Schumer, who has directly or indirectly overseen his party’s Senate campaign arm in almost every election cycle over the last 20 years, has regained trust within his caucus, for now, as Democrats are hopeful of making gains in the midterm elections despite a difficult map that favors Republicans.
Allies of the New York Democrat say it’s a significant turnaround from last year, when the party was still reeling from major election losses.
A low point came in the spring of 2025, when the party’s base erupted at Schumer for voting to keep President Donald Trump’s government open.
Interviews with more than a dozen Democratic senators in recent weeks indicate that Schumer has recovered his political standing with many in his caucus.
If Democrats gain seats in the election, colleagues expect him to easily win enough support in the closed-door leadership election, likely the week after Election Day.
Should they win a majority, a feat once seen as improbable, another term as leader would be nearly assured, many said.
Both parties pick their Senate leaders by secret ballot, so no senator has to reveal their vote.
Still, nothing is guaranteed.
While no Democrat has stepped up to challenge Schumer, that could quickly change if his party suffers an unexpected level of losses.
And several Democratic candidates around the country have said publicly that they won’t vote for Schumer or have remained noncommittal.
Interviewed by The Associated Press earlier this month, Schumer stated unequivocally that he’s running for another term as leader.
He said he believes Democrats have won more favor with voters over the last year and have a shot at winning the majority after fighting Trump’s tariffs, forcing more than a dozen votes to end the war in Iran and focusing on affordability, corruption and healthcare.
“I think our caucus is strong, it’s united,” Schumer said.
“A year ago, everyone said it was out of reach.
Today, we have a broader map, strong candidates, a clear contrast.”
Sen.
Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., said that “Senate seats in some ruby red states seem to be in play” because of candidates Schumer recruited.
Oregon Sen.
Ron Wyden, a Democrat who has served with Schumer for almost 30 years, said that “if you had told us in 2025 that we’d be in the home stretch with a really good shot of taking the majority, it would have been like, ‘You’ve got to be kidding me.’ You can’t argue with results.”
And if Democrats don’t win additional seats?
“I’m not thinking about that,” Wyden said.
Some senators won’t commit to supporting Schumer
While Schumer appears to be in a good position at the moment, many Democratic senators won’t say publicly whether they will support him — particularly those in the most progressive wing of the party.
“It’s a little bit too early to speculate on that right now,” said Sen.
Bernie Sanders, a Vermont independent who caucuses with Democrats.
Massachusetts Sen.
Elizabeth Warren said she is focused on November’s elections.
“We’ll know a lot more after the midterms,” she said.
Freshman Sen.
Elissa Slotkin of Michigan has called for a “new generation” of leaders across the party.
“It’s not a secret that Democrats still haven’t totally found their footing after Trump,” Slotkin said in a recent interview, adding that “we have to see what the results of the election are.”

Many are instead eyeing runs for the White House in 2028.

2 leadership spot to replace retiring Illinois Sen.
Dick Durbin.

Schumer backed El-Sayed’s primary opponent, but the two met in Washington last month.
El-Sayed said after the meeting that the party is united and “we’re having really productive conversations about what it takes to win.”
Schumer has kept his caucus close
Several of the Democratic senators who insisted on anonymity to share their views agreed that Schumer is likely to win another term as leader.

A commitment like that could end the conversation, one senator said.

All of the senators agreed that there are no obvious contenders right now to challenge him, but that could change quickly if Democrats lose Senate seats in November.
Schumer has turned the tables since 2025
Attitudes within the Democratic caucus have improved since last year, when the base revolted against Schumer for the March vote to keep the Republican president’s government open.
Progressive groups like MoveOn called for him to step down, arguing that Democrats needed to fight harder against Trump and Republicans.
Schumer regained some favor with Democrats inside and outside the Capitol during a prolonged government shutdown a year ago and as he has repeatedly blocked Trump’s nominees and Republican legislation.
But while the calls to resign or step aside have waned, many are still agitating for change.
“Our priority right now is organizing and making sure we elect a new generation laser-focused on affordability and fighting corruption,” said Joel Payne, a national spokesman for MoveOn.
Referring to the 2025 calls for Schumer to step aside, Payne said the group’s members have “already rendered a judgment on Schumer’s tenure and made clear they’re eager for new leadership that energizes the party base.”
It’s unclear, though, whether calls from the progressive wing of the party will influence the secret ballot vote, in which Schumer needs only a majority to win.
Sen.
Ben Ray Lujan, D-N.M., dismissed the talk about Schumer’s future.
“It’s hard to lose if no one else is challenging you,” he said.

All of the senators agreed that there are no obvious contenders right now to challenge him, but that could change quickly if Democrats lose Senate seats in November.
Schumer has turned the tables since 2025
Attitudes within the Democratic caucus have improved since last year, when the base revolted against Schumer for the March vote to keep the Republican president's government open.
Progressive groups like MoveOn called for him to step down, arguing that Democrats needed to fight harder against Trump and Republicans.
Schumer regained some favor with Democrats inside and outside the Capitol during a prolonged government shutdown a year ago and as he has repeatedly blocked Trump’s nominees and Republican legislation.
But while the calls to resign or step aside have waned, many are still agitating for change.
“Our priority right now is organizing and making sure we elect a new generation laser-focused on affordability and fighting corruption,” said Joel Payne, a national spokesman for MoveOn.
Referring to the 2025 calls for Schumer to step aside, Payne said the group’s members have “already rendered a judgment on Schumer’s tenure and made clear they’re eager for new leadership that energizes the party base.”
It’s unclear, though, whether calls from the progressive wing of the party will influence the secret ballot vote, in which Schumer needs only a majority to win.
Sen.
Ben Ray Lujan, D-N.M., dismissed the talk about Schumer’s future.
“It’s hard to lose if no one else is challenging you,” he said.

New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is leaving her job after just five days in the face of criticism over her performance, a White House official confirmed to CNBC on Friday.
Earlier Friday afternoon, President Donald Trump told reporters that he had just suggested to Zacharia that she quit.
"I just spoke to her about it.
I said, 'Katie, is this for you?'" Trump said outside the White House.
"'If I were you, I'd reconsider,'" the president said he told Zacharia.
The White House official, who asked not to be named in order to discuss the staffing shake-up, confirmed Fox News' report that Zacharia is "transitioning" out of the press secretary role.
Zacharia's five-day tenure in the Trump administration is shorter than that of Anthony Scaramucci, who in 2017 served as White House communications director for less than 11 days.
That length of time became jokingly referred to as a "Scaramucci" and was used to measure the durations of other officials who served briefly.
By that metric, Zacharia lasted one-half of one Scaramucci.
"Records are made to be broken.
But I take no pleasure in other people's pain," Scaramucci said in an X post later Friday.
Zacharia, a conservative commentator who worked at Trump Media & Technology Group, had faced widespread criticism in the days since she led a short and shaky first press briefing.
She also came under mounting scrutiny about her legal background.
Trump spoke to reporters before heading to Georgia for a political rally as he hopes to boost Republicans' electoral chances with just 18 days until the midterms.
But Trump's efforts to sell his agenda have been muddled in part by Zacharia, who ended her first, and only, press briefing on Tuesday after delivering halting remarks and taking questions from just three reporters.
In the less than six minutes she spent answering questions, Zacharia revealed that U.S.
Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle had been asked to step down.
That departure, and Zacharia's, follow those of a number of other high-ranking female officials in the Trump administration who have quit or been fired in recent months.
"You know, she's been treated very rough.
And she's a nice person," Trump said of Zacharia outside the White House.
He accused the media of treating her "very badly" and said that even Fox News TV host Sean Hannity, a supporter of the administration, was "a little bit tough" on Zacharia during her appearance on his show Thursday night.
Hannity, after calling Zacharia's debut briefing "widely panned," had asked about her past claims about her legal work in light of reports that she never passed a bar exam.
Zacharia has defended identifying herself as a lawyer, drawing a distinction between that label and calling herself an "attorney."
Hannity pointed out that Zacharia had called herself an attorney in multiple social media posts.
"I think they were retweets, and I corrected the record," she replied.
Trump called Zacharia "an attorney" in his Oct.
9 Truth Social post announcing her selection to replace Karoline Leavitt, who left the Trump administration in late August.
Zacharia's first day was Columbus Day.
White House officials had defended Zacharia earlier this week.
"Up and down the White House, everyone has been thoroughly impressed with Katie in just a few short days on the job," White House communications director Steven Cheung said in an X post Wednesday.
"At the end of this second term, she'll be remembered as one of the all-time greats," Cheung wrote.
CNN chief White House correspondent Kaitlan Collins, however, reported Friday that Trump was "embarrassed by the coverage of Zacharia's briefing and when he polled other aides about her, Zacharia had few allies willing to stand up for her or defend her performance."
"She's been treated, I would say, pretty nastily," Trump said of Zacharia in Friday's remarks outside the White House.
"And I said to Katie just two minutes ago, I said, 'Katie, you know, you don't have to do this if you don't want.'"
Asked if he would keep her in the role, Trump said, "I'm going to let her make that decision."

The White House Press Secretary is a senior White House official whose primary responsibility is to act as spokesperson for the executive branch of the United States federal government, especially with regard to the president, senior aides and executives, as well as government policies.
The press secretary is responsible for collecting information about actions and events within the president's administration and issues the administration's reactions to developments around the world.
The press secretary interacts with the media and the White House press corps on a daily basis, generally in a daily press briefing.
The press secretary serves by the appointment and at the pleasure of the president of the United States; the office does not require the advice and consent of the United States Senate; however, because of the frequent briefings given to the global media, who in turn inform the public, the position is a prominent non-Cabinet post.
Katie Zacharia is the most recent White House press secretary, but the position has been vacant since October 16, 2026 after Zacharia's firing five days after taking the position.
History
[edit]
Early press relations
[edit]
In the United States' early years, there was no single designated staff person or office responsible for managing the relationship between the president and the growing number of journalists and media entities that were covering him.[2] It was not until after President Abraham Lincoln's administration that Congress formally appropriated funds for a White House staff, which at first consisted merely of a secretary.
Ulysses S.
Grant's White House staff officially numbered six people at a cost of $13,800, though he supplemented with personnel from the War Department.
Fifty years later under the Coolidge administration, the staff had increased to just fewer than fifty people at a cost of nearly $100,000.[2]
As presidents increasingly hired more staff, some showed a tendency to pick aides and confidantes who had backgrounds in journalism.[2] One of Abraham Lincoln's private secretaries, John G.
Nicolay, had been an editor and owner of a newspaper in Illinois before he worked for the president in the White House.[3] While the modern equivalent of a private or personal secretary to the president of the United States would be more narrowly concerned with the care and feeding of the president,[4] the small size of the White House staff at that point meant that Nicolay interacted with the press occasionally in carrying out his duties.[3] He was occasionally asked to verify stories or information that various members of the press had heard.[3] Though the title and establishment of the roles and responsibilities of the press secretary job was still decades in the future, the small and growing White House staff was increasingly interacting with a growing number of professional journalists and mass media entities covering the president and the White House.[3] Andrew Johnson was the first president to grant a formal interview request to a reporter, sitting down with Col.
Alexander K.
McClure from Pennsylvania.[5] Although various presidents and reporters had participated in conversations or dialogues prior to Johnson, the exchanges had been less formal.[6]
Cleveland and McKinley administrations
[edit]
Prior to the 1880s and the presidency of Grover Cleveland, the relationship between the president, his administration, and the small but growing number of newspapers covering him was such that there was little need for a formal plan or designated spokesperson to manage it.[2] The relationship between government and the press was not as inherently adversarial and arms length as in modern times.
In fact, prior to the establishment of the U.S.
Government Printing Office (GPO), some newspapers were awarded contracts to print government publications and often supported the president in exchange.[2] For example, the Gazette of the United States won an early U.S.
Treasury contract and was supportive of President George Washington.[5] In general, though coverage of the president could be harsh and opinionated, newspapers were to some degree extensions of the political party apparatus and subsequently not seen as entities requiring specific, sustained management by the White House or administration.
The media had changed significantly by 1884, when Grover Cleveland was elected as president of the United States.
Between 1776 and 1884, the United States had quadrupled geographically and increased in population from 2.5 million to 56 million.[5] The number of newspaper publications in active circulation had increased from 37 to more than 1,200 dailies, in addition to the many new monthly magazines.[5] The rapid growth in journalism as a booming industry resulted in an increase in reporters covering the activities of the president.[7]
Grover Cleveland married 21-year-old Frances Folsom in 1886.
The growing number of reporters and the increasing aggressiveness of their style of coverage led to frustrations when the president and his new bride were unable to rid themselves of reporters who followed them to their honeymoon in Deer Park, Maryland.[7] President Cleveland relied on his private secretary, Daniel Lamont, who had once been an editor of the Albany Argus, to keep the reporters at bay.[7] The controversy surrounding coverage of the trip resulted in a public debate about the balance between the right of the president and his family to privacy and the role of the press in covering the country's most public figure.[8] In an editorial, the New York World defended the right of the press to cover the president at all times:
The idea of offending the bachelor sensitiveness of President Cleveland or the maidenly reserve of his bride has been far from anybody's thought...We must insist that the President is public property; that it is perfectly legitimate to send correspondents and reporters to follow him when he goes on a journey, and to keep watch over him and his family.[8]
White House press corps
[edit]
At the end of the Cleveland administration, a new feature of press coverage of the White House materialized.
William W.
Price, a southern reporter, auditioned for a job at the Washington Evening Star by stationing himself at the White House to seek out stories.[9] He interviewed guests coming and going from meetings or events with the president and ultimately reported a story in a piece carrying the headline "At the White House".[9] Competitor newspapers responded by sending their own reporters to cover the White House in a daily, sustained way and soon the White House had reporters dedicated to covering the "White House beat".
Some point to this as the early origins of a more formal White House Press Corps.[9]
When President Cleveland was elected to a second, non-consecutive term in 1893, George B.
Cortelyou, formally trained as a stenographer, was named confidential stenographer at the White House and later named executive clerk.[10] Though he was not given the formal title of private secretary to the president until later and the term press secretary had not yet been conceived, Cortelyou was highly respected by the press and William McKinley's biographer, Margaret Leach, called Cortelyou "the first of the presidential press secretaries".[10] President Cleveland's successor, William McKinley, kept Cortelyou on during the transition and later formally named him private secretary to the president, though he had been informally doing the job for some time prior.[11] Under McKinley, Cortelyou became notable for his popularity with journalists covering the White House.[12] The correspondents

Anna Kelly (born 1996) is an American spokesperson who has served as the White House principal deputy press secretary since February 2026.
Early life and education
[edit]
Anna Kelly was born in 1996.[1][2] Kelly graduated from Auburn University with a bachelor's degree in political science in 2017 and later earned a master's in political management from George Washington University.[3] Kelly applied as a White House intern in the first Trump administration in her senior year.[4] She won the Miss State Fair of Virginia in 2019.[1]
Career
[edit]
Spokesperson work (2020–2024)
[edit]
By May 2020, Kelly had become a spokesperson for Donald Trump's 2020 presidential campaign in Wisconsin.[5] Following the election, she was the communications director of the Republican Party of Wisconsin from January 2021 to August 2022.
By October 2022, she had become a spokesperson for Tim Michels, the Republican candidate in that year's Wisconsin gubernatorial election;[6] by July 2023, a spokesperson for Wisconsin representative Derrick Van Orden;[6] and by January 2024 was national press secretary for the Republican National Committee.[7] After Trump won the 2024 presidential election, Kelly became a spokesperson for his presidential transition.[8]
White House Office of the Press Secretary (2025–present)
[edit]
On January 25, 2025, Trump named Kelly as a White House deputy press secretary.[9] By February 2026, she had become the White House principal deputy press secretary.[10] Kelly was one of several aides who accompanied Trump on his visit to China in May.[11] After Karoline Leavitt, the White House press secretary, announced that she would resign in August, Kelly was considered a possible candidate to succeed her.[a] According to Politico, Kelly had been suggested as a candidate internally.[16]

manifold-QC80ENZPh5.text:
Florida Republican Senator Ashley Moody’s campaign team on Friday sent a “special election alert” email to supporters, warning her election battle with Democrat Angie Nixon is now a “dead heat,” according to two recent opinion polls.
If Nixon, currently a Florida state representative, can flip the seat formerly held by Marco Rubio, it would be a big win for the Democrats and their quest to seize control of the Senate at the November midterms.
No Democrat has won statewide in Florida since 2018 and Republicans enjoy a big voter registration advantage.
In their email, the Moody campaign team wrote: “Two polls.
Two dead heats.
Trump-backed Ashley Moody is tied with Angie Nixon in the biggest Senate special election of 2026 – for the seat Marco Rubio held for fourteen years.”
The two surveys cited in the email, which found Moody and Nixon were near level pegging, were conducted by St.
Pete Polls and Change Research.
New Polls
The St.
Pete Polls survey of 913 likely Florida voters found Moody ahead by just 0.4 percentage points, with 45.2 percent against her Democratic challenger's 44.8 percent.
The poll was conducted from September 15 to 17 using automated telephone calls and peer-to-peer SMS messages and had a margin of error of plus or minus 3.2 percentage points.
It showed Nixon leading with independents by 49.8 percent against 37.4 percent, and by voters aged 18 to 29 by 63.7 percent to 25.3 percent.
By contrast, Moody was ahead with non-Hispanic white voters by 53.4 percent to 38.7 percent, and those aged 70 or older with 61.1 percent to 31.9 percent.
These details should be treated with caution due to the small sample sizes once the survey was broken down by demographics.
Separately, Change Research surveyed 1,107 likely Florida voters for Freedom Project USA between September 7 and 9.
This poll found Moody and Nixon were tied with 47 percent of the vote each, while President Trump had a net favorability rating of minus ten.
It had a margin of error of plus or minus 2.8 percentage points.
However, a separate Quantus Insights poll of 733 likely Florida voters put Moody ahead with 50 percent of the vote against 43 percent.
This was conducted between September 8 and 10 and had a 4.1 percentage point margin of error.
Newsweek contacted the Moody and Nixon campaigns for comment on Saturday outside of regular office hours via online inquiry form and email respectively.
The recent tied polls are particularly notable as at the end of July Republicans had around 1.5 million more voters registered in Florida than Democrats, whilst Trump won the state by 13 points in 2024.
Republican Senate candidates outperformed their Democratic rivals by 12.8 percent in 2024 and 16.4 percent in 2022.
Despite the recent polling lead, Moody remains the firm favorite according to election analysis website Decision Desk HQ, which gives her a 78 percent probability of victory.
A RealClearPolling average of recent surveys gives Moody a five-point lead, with 48.3 percent of the vote against 43.3 percent for Nixon.
Primary Shock
Moody was appointed to the Senate in January 2025 by Florida Governor Ron DeSantis occupying the seat formerly held by Rubio, Trump’s pick for Secretary of State.
Nixon defeated Alexander Vindman, a retired army lieutenant colonel, to secure the Democratic nomination to challenge Moody at a primary election on August 18.
This was a major upset, with Vindman significantly outspending Nixon, a social democrat, in the contest.
Currently, there are 53 Republican Senators versus 47 who caucus with the Democrats.
Losing the Senate in November would significantly impede Trump’s freedom of action in the final two years of his term.

That was just ten days after launch.
What Muse does and how fast it spread
Meta launched Muse on September 8, 2026, for users aged 18 and older in the US.
The pitch is an agent, not a chatbot.
A chatbot answers questions, while an agent is meant to go do things on your behalf.
Muse is built to handle tasks like booking reservations, managing email, and working toward user goals across services such as Gmail and Spotify.
Cumulative US downloads passed 5 million within 22 days of launch, according to Sensor Tower.
Estimates put Muse’s daily active users at around 700,000 by late September 2026.
The app was also reportedly handling over 1 million daily prompts.
Five million downloads against roughly 700,000 daily users means most people who installed Muse are not opening it on any given day.
The retention problem
Muse’s open rates sit significantly below those of established apps like ChatGPT and Instagram, which points to a retention challenge.

Growing pains on the infrastructure side

How Meta plans to make money

The company has invested heavily in AI, and a No.
1 app gives investors something tangible to point at amid rising competition from other AI products.

Meta's Muse AI personal agent tool has only been out for nearly two weeks, and it's topping the app store charts.
as of Monday.
It's also ahead of rival AI apps like Anthropic's Claude and SpaceXAI's Grok AI, in addition to the Facebook-parent's own Meta AI app.
The Muse app overtook ChatGPT as the leading iOS free app in the U.S.
on Friday, and racked up 730,000 downloads over about five days after it launched on Sep.
8, according to the analytics firm Sensor Tower.
As of Monday, Muse has logged over 2.5 million downloads since its debut, the market intelligence company said.
Muse's cumulative downloads topped Claude and Grok during the same 13-day post-launch window, with those apps recording 400,000 and 200,000 downloads, respectively.
ChatGPT obtained 3.1 million downloads during that time frame, Sensor Tower said.
The firm noted that the apps had staggered platform releases split between Apple and Google Play, which would impact their totals.
Sensor Tower said that as of Monday, Muse has garnered around 1.5 million and 1.1 million downloads on the iOS and Android app stores, respectively.
Meta pitched the app as a way for consumers to manage and direct supercharged digital assistants that can perform a number of tasks across the web, like filling out electronic forms and organizing email inboxes.
The app, which is powered by Meta's Muse Spark family of AI models, represents a major push by CEO Mark Zuckerberg into the AI agent market, which the freely available OpenClaw tool helped popularize earlier this year among developers and technology enthusiasts.
"I think up to this point most of the agentic use cases have not really been for normal people," Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon told CNBC in a "Squawk on the Street" interview on Monday.
"Now you've got Meta's Muse and other agents out there that are starting to maybe get more potential for more broad-based adoption."
The buzz around Meta was also reflected in the stock, which surged more than 11% on Monday.
Wells Fargo lifted its price target on the company's stock to $796, according to multiple reports.
Although people can use the Muse app for free, Meta is also offering monthly subscriptions that will cost $20 or $100, depending on usage.
It's a way for Meta to potentially make money off AI agents that isn't centered on the company's core online advertising business.
But Meta's debut of Muse comes amid broader societal concerns around AI's safety and cybersecurity risks that have rocked the tech industry over the past few weeks.
Meta also recently agreed to pay roughly $17 billion to settle with a coalition of state attorneys general that had sued the company for misrepresenting alleged harms to children and teenagers caused by apps like Facebook and Instagram.
It's unclear how long the Muse app will remain a hit, considering that other AI services have experienced similar boom times upon their release but failed to remain blockbusters, such as OpenAI's Sora and Meta's Vibes AI video tool, which helped bolster downloads of the Meta AI app when it was first launched last September.
"They care about security, I don't know how much they care about privacy," Rasgon said, referring to whether the personal data-hungry Muse app will sting Meta in the long run.
The growing popularity of these agents is having ripple effects on the places they visit online, and e-commerce giant Amazon has blocked Muse from accessing its shopping site, citing privacy and security risks.
Amazon said it was not given advanced notice that Muse would access its store and outlined several other concerns.
The company said the agent bypasses the personalization and other features built into the shopping experience and said Muse appears to capture and store customer credentials and scrape account data.
"We think it's fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate," an Amazon spokesperson said in a statement.
GeekWire was first to report on the move by Amazon.
Shopify, however, is working with Meta on Muse access.
Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke announced Monday that the e-commerce site was partnering with Muse to allow agentic checkout in its online stores.

(WCAX) - A new poll shows New Hampshire Gov.

Gov.
Ayotte, a well-known incumbent, faces a challenge from Warmington, a former executive councilor who is appearing on a statewide general election ballot for the first time.
“I wake up every day looking to make New Hampshire more affordable for the people of this state,” Ayotte said.
She says she’s running for re-election on her record, citing a bunch of bills she signed into law during her first term.
“I signed bail reform, getting the cellphones out of the schools, a dozen bills to increase housing,” Ayotte said.
But Cinde Warmington says it’s time for a change.
“I’m running for office because the people of New Hampshire really need a change of direction,” she said.
Warmington served four years on the New Hampshire Executive Council, which acts as a check and balance for the governor.
She says the race is about pocketbooks and rising prices.
If elected, she says she’ll suspend the state gas tax and push for consumer refunds on tariffs.
“Kelly Ayotte has driven up the cost of housing, the cost of electricity, the cost of health care in our state,” she said.
“She and I just have a very different philosophy when it comes to cost,” said Ayotte, who points to cost-cutting measures like child care tax credits she supported and rural health transformation grants that are being rolled out.
“My opponent wants to bring Massachusetts-style policies here to New Hampshire, which means increasing taxes.”
Related Story:
Both candidates took “The Pledge” — a promise not to support a broad-based sales or income tax.
“There is no way we could put an additional tax burden on the working people of our state.
I will not do it.
To think you need to solve this problem with taxes is a failure of imagination,” Warmington said.
When it comes to name recognition, Ayotte has the clear advantage.
She’s a former state attorney general and represented New Hampshire as a U.S.
senator.
Warmington practiced health care law for two decades.
She ran for governor in 2024 but lost in her party’s primary.
“Yeah, experience-wise, I think it shows -- her record -- that she has a long record of failure,” Warmington said.
Warmington has been criticized for her previous work lobbying on behalf of the pharmaceutical industry.
“Her qualifications and mine could not be more different.
While she was doing that, I was at the AG’s office prosecuting crimes, prosecuting murder cases,” Ayotte said.
“Kelly Ayotte wants to stay focused on things my clients did 25 years ago.
I am going to stay 100% focused on the people of the Granite State,” Warmington said.
Ayotte has consistently led in the polls, but the race will likely be decided by independent or undeclared voters, the largest voting bloc in the Granite State.

—Who decides.

—Why Americans care.

Brazil’s central bank interest rate, the Selic, is 13.75% a year as of 19 October 2026, after a quarter-point cut on 16 September.
At that rate R$1,000 (about US$197 at R$5.07 per dollar on 19 October) earns roughly R$137.50 (about US$27) over a year, before tax.

Checked Oct 26, 10:15 UTC.
What the Selic Rate Is
The Selic is Brazil’s benchmark interest rate, the price of overnight money between banks.
It plays the role of the US federal funds rate, and every loan, savings product and government bond in Brazil is priced from it.
The name comes from the Special System for Settlement and Custody, the platform where federal bonds trade.
The central bank publishes a target rate after each meeting and a slightly lower “effective” rate that banks actually pay.
Why US Readers Should Care
For a dollar investor, the Selic is the reward for holding Brazil.
With US rates at 3.75% to 4.00%, the gap of about 10 percentage points attracts “carry trade” money, which borrows in cheap dollars to earn Brazilian yields.
That money supports the real, but it can leave fast if the central bank cuts too quickly or politics frighten investors.
The same rate shapes the profits of US-listed Brazilian companies such as Petrobras (PBR), Vale (VALE), Itaú (ITUB) and Nubank (NU), and the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ).
A high Selic also raises the cost of credit for Brazilian families and firms, which is why cuts tend to help rate-sensitive sectors such as retail and construction.
For travellers and expats paid in dollars, a higher rate usually means a stronger real and costlier Brazil.
How a Copom Decision Works
Copom is made up of the governor and the directors of the Banco Central do Brasil, and each member has one vote.
It meets over two days, usually Tuesday and Wednesday, and announces the decision on Wednesday evening after about 6:30 p.m.
Brasília time.
The inflation target is 3.0% with a tolerance band of 1.5 points either side, so 1.5% to 4.5%.
When inflation runs above the band the committee holds or raises rates, and it cuts when prices cool.
Brazil’s real interest rate, the Selic minus inflation, is about 8.8% using the 12-month IPCA of 4.58% for September.
That gap is the main reason the committee says policy must stay tight.

The cycle began on 18 March 2026, when the rate fell from 15.00%.
What Moved the Rate Lately
- 16 September: the committee cut to 13.75% hours after the Fed moved the other way.
Our report on the decision covers the split verdict between the two banks.
- 22 September: the minutes said inflation is still driven by demand, so policy must stay tight.
Read the minutes explained.
- 9 October: September inflation rose to 4.58%, above the 4.5% ceiling of the target band.
See the inflation report, and how economists now expect 5.22% for 2026.
What Comes Next
The Focus survey, a weekly poll of banks and funds run by the central bank, expected in its 13 October edition that the Selic would end 2026 at 13.25%, which implies about two more quarter-point cuts.
That is a forecast, not a promise, and the committee has declined to commit to a path.

How Foreigners Can Earn the Selic
Brazilian residents buy Tesouro Selic, a federal bond that pays the Selic, through the Treasury’s Tesouro Direto platform.
Bank certificates of deposit (CDBs) pay a share of the CDI, the interbank rate that tracks the Selic.
Non-residents invest through a local custodian under separate central bank rules, and their tax treatment differs from the 15% to 22.5% schedule that residents pay.

Data sources
All data collected automatically from public databases of the Central Bank of Brazil, with no manual intervention:
- Selic target and decision history: Time Series Management System (SGS), series 432 — the COPOM Selic target.
- CDI: SGS series 4389 (annualized DI rate).
- IPCA accumulated over 12 months: SGS series 433.
- Meeting calendar: official COPOM schedule published by the Central Bank.
- Market expectations: Focus Bulletin of the Central Bank — a weekly survey of more than 130 financial institutions; we use the median projection for the Selic at the next meeting.
This is not the site's opinion: it is the market consensus measured by the Central Bank.
When the page updates
On normal days, once a day.
On COPOM decision days (always a Wednesday), the server polls the Central Bank periodically late in the afternoon and, as soon as the new rate is published, updates this page and sends a notification to all users informing them whether the Selic was hiked, cut, or held.
The Selic target (set by COPOM) is the policy reference.
The Selic over (effective rate) typically sits a few basis points below the target on a day-to-day basis.

The Selic is the benchmark rate set by Brazil's central bank; the CDI is the interbank lending rate, which tracks it closely and sits slightly below.

Expectativa para a Selic no fim de 2026 continua em 13,25% no Focus do BC
A mediana das expectativas do mercado financeiro no relatório Focus do Banco Central para a taxa Selic no fim de 2026 seguiu em 13,25%.
Considerando só as 60 estimativas atualizadas nos últimos cinco dias úteis, mais sensíveis a novidades, a mediana para a Selic no fim deste ano também permaneceu em 13,25%.
Já a estimativa intermediária do relatório Focus para a taxa Selic no fim de 2027 ficou em 12,00% pela 18ª semana consecutiva.
Levando em conta apenas as 59 estimativas atualizadas nos últimos cinco dias úteis, a mediana aumentou de 11,75% para 12,00%.
Em 16 de setembro, o Comitê de Política Monetária (Copom) do Banco Central reduziu a Selic em mais 0,25 ponto porcentual, de 14,00% para 13,75% ao ano.
Foi o quinto corte consecutivo dos juros.
A Selic já caiu 1,25 ponto porcentual desde março, quando o BC começou um "ciclo de calibração" da política monetária, em meio às incertezas sobre os impactos da guerra do Irã na cadeia global de suprimentos, nos preços de commodities e na própria inflação.
"O cenário atual, caracterizado por significativo aumento da incerteza, desancoragem das expectativas e riscos elevados em torno do cenário base, demanda serenidade e cautela na condução da política monetária.
O Comitê seguirá incorporando novas informações e acompanhando a evolução do cenário de forma a manter a restrição adequada para assegurar a convergência da inflação à meta", disse o Copom na ata da reunião.
A mediana do mercado para a Selic no fim de 2028 ficou em 10,50% pela 16ª semana seguida.
A estimativa para 2029 continuou em 10,00% pela 24ª semana consecutiva.

An open-weight model built by a Chinese AI lab just did something no open model had done before.
Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 on July 16, 2026, packing 2.8 trillion parameters and a 1-million-token context window, and just three months later, on October 12, 2026, it climbed to the top of LMArena’s Frontend Code Arena with an Elo score of 1,679, edging past OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol at 1,618.
It is the first time an openly released model has outright led that particular coding leaderboard, rather than trailing just behind the proprietary frontier.
For a market that has spent two years assuming the best coding models would always sit behind a paywall, that is a real shift, not a rounding error.
The result lands in the middle of a crowded year for AI model releases.
Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI have all shipped new flagship systems since the summer, and Chinese labs including DeepSeek, Alibaba’s Qwen team, and Tencent have kept pace with their own open releases.
Kimi K3’s leaderboard finish adds a new data point to that race, and it raises a practical question for any team choosing a model today: is paying per token for a closed frontier model still worth it when a free-to-download alternative tops the chart on the exact benchmark that matters for coding work?

What Happened: Kimi K3 Takes the Top Coding Spot
LMArena runs crowdsourced, head-to-head comparisons where real users vote on which of two anonymous model outputs they prefer, then converts those votes into a chess-style Elo rating.
The Frontend Code Arena is a specialized slice of that system focused on front-end coding tasks, the kind of work developers actually do when building interfaces rather than solving abstract algorithm puzzles.
According to a benchmark comparison published by CodersEra, Kimi K3 posted a 1,679 Elo score on that board, placing it ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol’s 1,618 in the same snapshot.
That 61-point gap is not enormous by Elo standards, but the identity of the model sitting at number one is the story.
Coding leaderboards on LMArena have historically been dominated by proprietary systems from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, with open-weight entrants from Mistral or Meta usually landing a few spots lower.
Kimi K3 breaking that pattern outright, rather than just closing the gap, is what separates this result from the steady incremental narrowing the industry has watched for the past year.
Kimi K3 also posted a general text Elo score of roughly 1,500 on LMArena’s broader leaderboard, a figure that puts it in the same neighborhood as several proprietary frontier systems rather than trailing them by a wide margin.
That dual showing, strong on a specialized coding board and competitive on the general leaderboard, is part of why the release drew attention beyond the usual circle of open-model watchers.
Who Is Moonshot AI?
From Kimi K2.6 to K3
Moonshot AI is a Beijing-based AI lab that has built its Kimi family of models over the past two years, releasing successive versions at a pace that mirrors the broader Chinese open-model push covered in Jack Clark’s recent Import AI newsletter.
A public model-tracking repository lists Kimi K2.6 as added on April 20, 2026, with Kimi K3 following on July 16, 2026, making K3 the newer generation in a lineage that has moved quickly even by this industry’s standards.
That cadence matters for context.
Moonshot did not leapfrog the field with a single lucky release.
It shipped K2.6, gathered feedback and benchmark data, then pushed out K3 roughly three months later with enough of a capability jump to take the top coding spot.
Tencent followed a similar playbook with its Hy4 model narrowly edging out GLM-5.3 on a separate set of benchmarks, suggesting Chinese labs are increasingly treating rapid, iterative open releases as a core competitive strategy rather than an occasional showcase.
Being open-weight means Moonshot publishes the model’s parameters so anyone can download, run, and fine-tune it without going through a paid API, subject to the license terms Moonshot attaches.
That is a fundamentally different distribution model from the one OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google use for their top-tier systems, and it is the detail that turns a leaderboard score into a business story.
Inside the Numbers: What the Leaderboard Snapshot Shows
Reading an Elo leaderboard requires a little care.
The scores are relative, not absolute, and they shift as new models enter the comparison pool and as voting volume grows.
Still, the October 2026 snapshot gives a useful picture of where the top systems stood heading into the back half of the year, both on the specialized coding board and on LMArena’s general text arena.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kimi K3 | Moonshot AI | Open-weight | Frontend Code Arena | 1,679 |
| GPT-6.1 Sol | OpenAI | Proprietary | Frontend Code Arena | 1,618 |

Three of the five rows in that table belong to open-weight models, and all three come from Chinese labs.
That clustering is not an accident.
DeepSeek, Alibaba’s Qwen team, and Moonshot have each released multiple model generations in 2026, and all three now show up within roughly 200 Elo points of each other on the general leaderboard, which is a tight band for models built by separate teams with separate training pipelines.
Why an Open Model Beating Proprietary Systems Matters
Benchmark leadership by itself does not automatically translate into adoption.
Enterprises weigh support contracts, uptime guarantees, and fine-tuning tooling alongside raw capability.
But a coding leaderboard is a benchmark that developers actually feel in daily use, unlike more abstract reasoning tests.
When the top-ranked front-end coding model is something a team can download and run on its own infrastructure, the calculus around build-versus-buy shifts in a very concrete way.
That shift plays out differently depending on who is asking the question.
A startup with tight margins and in-house ML infrastructure gains a real option to self-host a top-tier coding model instead of paying per-token API fees indefinitely.
A large enterprise with existing vendor relationships and compliance requirements may stick with a proprietary provider regardless, because procurement and support contracts carry weight that a leaderboard score does not capture.
Both groups, though, now have to factor an open-weight option into decisions they might previously have skipped straight past.
It also changes the pressure proprietary labs face on pricing.
OpenAI already cut prices sharply when it shipped GPT-6.1 Sol at a fifth of the cost of the model it replaced (its pricing page, updated October 16, 2026, reportedly lists GPT-6.1 Sol at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens), and Anthropic followed with a steep cut to Claude Haiku API pricing.
A credible open-weight challenger at the top of a widely watched leaderboard gives labs another reason to keep trimming margins rather than risk losing developer mindshare to a free alternative.
The Pricing Divide: Open Weights vs.
Per-Token Billing
The practical difference between Kimi K3 and its proprietary rivals shows up most clearly in how each one gets paid for.
OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google all charge by the token, with per-million-token rates that vary widely depending on which tier of model a developer selects.
Kimi K3, by contrast, can be downloaded and run on infrastructure a team already owns or rents, with no per-token fee tied to Moonshot itself, though compute costs for hosting a model of that size are real and not trivial.

LMArena Leaderboard October 2026: Where the Top Text Scores Stand
Gemini 4 Argon (High) tops Arena's text leaderboard on 1532 with style control off (20 October 2026).
What it means for the Arena score prediction.
versus Editorial · 28 September 2026
In Arena's text leaderboard update dated 20 October 2026, the highest overall score with style control turned off is 1532, held by Google's Gemini 4 Argon (High).
On the versus prediction about the best Arena score, the page showed 47.4p for the 1540 answer at 08:00 UK time on 21 October 2026, the market's estimate of a 47.4% chance that a model gets there before the cut-off.
LMArena, which now calls itself Arena, ranks AI models by people's votes: two anonymous models answer the same prompt and the voter picks the better answer.
The live prediction on versus has seven answers from 1520 to 1700 and asks whether any model reaches each score before a cut-off early on 1 January 2027.
A score of 1532 is above the 1520 and 1530 answers and 8 points short of 1540.
Arena and Its Score
According to its About page, Arena (formerly LMArena) was created by researchers from UC Berkeley and was previously known as Chatbot Arena.
The old lmarena.ai address now forwards to arena.ai.
Arena's FAQ says votes are turned into scores with the Bradley-Terry model, which it likens to the Elo ratings used in chess, and that only votes cast while the models are anonymous count.
What Style Control Changes
Arena's 2024 research on style found that the ranking changes once answer length and formatting (headers, bold text and lists) are taken into account, so the default view adjusts for them.
Under Adjustments you can also pick None, or Factuality, which Arena's post on factuality describes as a weighted mix of human preference and fact checks.
The prediction's rules ask for the score with style control turned off, and Arena's own address for the overall view without style control opens with None selected.
In the 20 October update Gemini 4 Argon (High) leads both the default view and the view without style control, on 1524 with style control on and 1532 with it off.
The order below it changes: Meta's Muse Wonder (Max) is second in the default view but sixth with style control off.
Where the Top Text Scores Stand in October 2026
The top five in the Text Arena overall ranking with style control turned off, in the update dated 20 October 2026, which the page says drew on 8,900,458 votes across 417 models:
- Gemini 4 Argon (High) (Google): 1532, ±9, from 4,900 votes.
- Claude Opus 5.5 (High) (Anthropic): 1516, ±7, from 9,496 votes.
- Claude Fable 5.1 (Max) (Anthropic): 1512, ±6.
- Claude Opus 5 (Max) (Anthropic): 1509, ±5.
- Claude Opus 5 (High) (Anthropic): 1503, ±4.
Arena's leaderboard changelog shows Gemini 4 Argon (High) joining the Text Arena on 30 September 2026; the models it added there on 2, 8, 13 and 20 October all sit outside the top five.
Google announced Argon on 30 September for trusted cyber defenders and opened it on 13 October 2026 to developers through its API and to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app; our Gemini 4 release date guide has the details.
Arena's leaderboard policy marks a score built on votes from before a model's public release as preliminary until enough fresh votes arrive afterwards.
Argon's score dates from before Google's public release on 13 October, so it falls under that rule until Arena has enough votes from after the release.
Its margin of ±9 on 4,900 votes compares with ±3 for Claude Opus 4.6 (High), seventh on 82,619 votes.
How This Prediction Settles
Every market on versus names the source that settles it before you trade.
This one's rules still use Arena's old names, Chatbot Arena and lmarena.ai, and point to the Score column of the Text Arena table, which opens on the overall ranking, read with style control turned off.
They say nothing about the Preliminary label.
Each number is a separate answer with its own price: if any model has reached at least that number by 05:59 Central European Time on Friday 1 January 2027, which is 04:59 UK time (GMT), a contract on it settles at 100p, and otherwise at 0p.
The page lists an earlier end date, 00:00 UK time (GMT) on Thursday 31 December 2026, when trading is due to stop (see when markets close).
If the leaderboard is down for a while, the prediction waits until it is back; if it disappears for good, the rules settle the prediction as No.
The answers are 1520, 1530, 1540, 1550, 1600, 1650 and 1700.
Because they are thresholds, several can be right: a top score of 1545 by the cut-off would make 1520, 1530 and 1540 right and the four higher answers wrong.
A higher number can never be more likely than a lower one, and the prices do not have to add up to 100p.
At 08:00 UK time on 21 October 2026 the versus page showed 32p for 1550 and 3.5p for 1700.
A Worked Example
Say the 1550 answer trades at 30p.
You put 600p into it, which buys 20 contracts.
The transaction fee is 2% of the stake, added on top, so it comes to 12p and 612p leaves your balance.
If a model reaches 1550 before the cut-off, the 20 contracts settle at 100p each, 2,000p in total.
If none does, they settle at 0p and the 612p is gone.
While the market is open you can sell at the current price: at 15p, the 20 contracts give you 300p back, a loss but a smaller one than 0p.
There is no leverage and no margin call, so the most the position can cost you is the 612p you saw before confirming.
Dates and Events That Could Move the Prices
- The next leaderboard update.
The page gave 20 October 2026 as its latest update when checked on 21 October, and Arena's changelog lists each model it adds.
- Fresh votes for Gemini 4 Argon (High).
Votes cast since Google's 13 October release can move its score either way.
- More Gemini 4 models.
Google says the rest of the Gemini 4 family will follow, with no names or dates.
- Thursday 31 December 2026, 00:00 UK time (GMT).
The end date listed on versus.
- Friday 1 January 2027, 04:59 UK time (GMT).
The cut-off in the rules for every answer.
Before you trade
Each answer settles at 100p if it comes true and at 0p if it does not, so you can lose the whole amount you put into a position; put in only what you are comfortable losing.

Frequently asked questions

In the update dated 20 October 2026 it is 1532, for Google's Gemini 4 Argon (High) with style control turned off.
In the default view, with style control on, the same model shows 1524.
Is the top score final?
No.
Argon was scored on Arena from 30 September 2026, before Google released it to the public on 13 October 2026, and Arena's policy treats such a score as preliminary until enough fresh votes arrive after the public release.
Which Arena view does the versus prediction use?
The one with style control turned off, which you get by choosing None under Adjustments on Arena's text leaderboard.
The default view gives the leader a different score, 1524 instead of 1532.
Can a model be removed from the Arena leaderboard?
Yes.
Under Arena's policy a model is removed if, for example, its API is not kept accessible for at least 30 days after launch.
The prediction's rules do not cover that case.

Israel’s Katz vows to strike Beirut’s southern suburbs over any rocket or drone fire
Defence minister threatens to expand southern occupation, acknowledges demolition of over 60 villages, 23,000 homes
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz warned Tuesday that any rocket or drone fire targeting Israel would prompt strikes on Beirut’s southern suburbs.
In a post on the US social media platform X, Katz said Israel could expand its occupation toward the Nabatieh and Litani areas if Lebanon’s Hezbollah group joined an Iranian attack.
He warned that residents of any newly seized territory would be evacuated and the areas permanently incorporated into what Israel calls its security zone in Lebanon.
Katz also ruled out an Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon until Hezbollah was disarmed throughout the country.
In an acknowledgment of the scale of destruction, Katz said Israeli forces had demolished more than 60 Lebanese villages containing 23,000 homes, claiming they had been used by Hezbollah for military purposes.
He further claimed that Israel had established a 700-square-kilometre security zone inside Lebanon and displaced around 200,000 residents.
Read: Peace in southern Lebanon remains ‘elusive’: UN mission
His remarks came as Lebanese and Israeli military delegations held United States-mediated talks at the US Central Command headquarters in Tampa, Florida on Tuesday.
Israel has carried out attacks on Lebanon since March 2, killing and injuring thousands of people and displacing over 1.5 million residents.
On June 26, Lebanon and Israel signed a US-sponsored framework agreement providing for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory, the deployment of the Lebanese army and the disarmament of Hezbollah.
Despite the agreement, Israel has continued its attacks on southern Lebanon.
Israeli forces also continue to occupy Lebanese territory, including areas held for decades and others seized during more recent wars and military operations.

BEIRUT — Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz on Wednesday threatened to empty and strike the southern suburb of Beirut and to expand Israeli occupation into southern Lebanon if Hezbollah joins Iran in attacking Israel amid rising tensions in the region.
Israel has not struck Beirut since early June, following the signing of a fragile cease-fire agreement and international pressure.
The Israeli army "is ready to launch a ground offensive" and Beirut's southern suburbs "will also be evacuated and its terrorist infrastructure struck, while more than a million Shiite residents will be displaced in Lebanon," Katz said during a visit Wednesday morning to Israeli-occupied areas of southern Lebanon.
"Nasrallah destroyed Lebanon's Shiite community before being eliminated, and Naim Qassem could wipe it out completely, until he too is eliminated," he added, referring to the former Hezbollah secretary-general, killed on Sept.
27, 2024, by an Israeli strike in Beirut, and to his successor.
On Tuesday night, he reported "attempts by our enemies, led by Iran and its proxies, to carry out attacks aimed at influencing the outcome of Israel's elections," according to Israeli media.
Several Israeli media outlets reported that Israel’s defense ministry and the U.S.
Pentagon signed an agreement Wednesday evening for the purchase of 12 advanced Boeing Apache attack helicopters for the Israeli army, following government approval earlier in the day.
The helicopters are scheduled for delivery early in the next decade, Israeli media reported.
They will be the AH-64E Apache variant, described by the defense ministry as the helicopter’s newest and most advanced model.
Netanyahu warns of attacks on Israel
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Wednesday in an interview with military radio station that "Israel's enemies are seeking to attack the country before the upcoming elections," scheduled for Oct.
27.
Asked about the possibility of a military escalation before the parliamentary elections, Netanyahu responded: "I sincerely hope that will not be the case."
"It is true that Israel's enemies want to attack us in the coming days, and there are signs to that effect," he added, while denying his statements were motivated by political considerations.
In a separate interview with Amir Ivgi on Israel’s Army Radio on Wednesday, Netanyahu said that Israel had completed most of its missions on the various fronts but still had objectives to achieve.
“We have done 90% of the work.
There is still more work to be done.
In the next two years, we will finally eliminate Hamas, destroy Hezbollah once and for all, and defeat Iran,” he said.
Separately, according to Haaretz on Wednesday, three people were injured in an explosion at an Intel factory in southern Israel, one of them critically.
Police suspect that a gas cylinder caused the explosion, while firefighters reported a leak of nitrogen trifluoride, a nonflammable gas with oxidizing properties.
Israel’s fire chief later said that the fire at the plant had been extinguished.
Meanwhile, Lebanese press reported Wednesday the arrival of an Iranian diplomatic delegation headed by Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh.
He was received by a delegation from the Amal Movement, led by Khalil Hamdane, who represented Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, as well as by Hezbollah MP Ali Mokdad.

JERUSALEM/BEIRUT — Israel said its military attacked Hezbollah targets in Beirut’s southern suburbs on Sunday after the Lebanese armed group fired into Israeli territory, and Lebanon’s Civil Defense Ministry said three people were killed.
The Israeli military said earlier that Hezbollah had launched three projectiles towards communities in northern Israel, calling it a blatant ceasefire violation.
“The IDF has now attacked terrorist targets of the Hezbollah terrorist organization in the Dahiyeh neighborhood of Beirut, in response to Hezbollah’s firing into Israeli territory,” a joint statement by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz said.
Three people were killed and six others wounded in the strike, which targeted an apartment in Dahiyeh, Lebanon’s Civil Defense Ministry said.
Lebanese security sources said the attack appeared to be a targeted strike with two missiles.
The Israeli military said it conducted a “precise” strike on a Hezbollah command centre.
There was no immediate comment from Hezbollah on the Israeli statements, but the group said it launched missiles and drones towards Israeli troops in southern Lebanon.
Last week, an Israeli strike on Dahiyeh triggered an exchange of fire between Israel and Iran that threatened to derail a U.S.-Iran deal that would end the wider war.
Washington and Tehran appear to be getting closer to a deal to end the more than three-month-long conflict, with U.S.
and Pakistani leaders forecast a signing on Sunday.
Iran has long made the cessation of fighting in Lebanon a condition for any wider agreement with the United States.
President Donald Trump said in a post on Truth Social Sunday that the strikes on Beirut “should not have happened, particularly on a special day when we are so close to a Peace Deal with Iran.”
“We are very close to a Deal that will bring peace to the region, including to Lebanon, and all sides should stand down.
There should be no more attacks by Israel anywhere in Lebanon,” he added.
The deputy commander of Iran’s top joint military command, Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, said on Sunday that Israeli “crimes” will not go unanswered, according to state media.
Iran’s top negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said on Sunday that Israel’s attack on Beirut’s southern suburbs showed the United States either lacked the will to fulfill its commitments or the ability to do so.
In a post on X, he said continuing on the current path would be impossible if commitments could not be fulfilled.
“Israel will not tolerate firing into its territory,” Netanyahu said in a post on X after the attack.
The Israeli military had issued a wide-scale evacuation warning earlier on Sunday for residents of at least 30 towns and villages in southern Lebanon.
Israeli forces have occupied swathes of southern Lebanon, and Israel says it is seeking to dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure on its borders.
Fighting with the Iran-backed group has not halted in the area despite the Lebanese government holding ceasefire talks with Israel in Washington.
Hezbollah has rejected the negotiations and said any ceasefire with Israel should secure an end to all hostilities, including in southern Lebanon and the withdrawal of Israeli troops.
Earlier this month, Israel said fighting in south Lebanon would continue and warned Lebanese residents against moving back to the south.
Hezbollah entered the war by firing at Israel on March 2, two days after the United States and Israel began airstrikes against Iran.
Israel said it would respond forcefully and has since carried out airstrikes that have killed thousands in Lebanon and displaced more than a million people.

Hezbollah has not commented on the blast.
Lebanon and Israel have held seven rounds of talks; the most recent took place in Rome earlier this month.
The Iran-backed Hezbollah has refused to disarm and accuses the Lebanese government of making too many concessions without guaranteeing an Israeli withdrawal.

Gunmen seize tanker off Yemen amid resurgence of Somali piracy
UK maritime security monitor says Seamull tanker was diverted toward Somalia, as growing wave of piracy sweeps the Gulf of Aden.
A tanker has been boarded by six armed people who took control of the vessel off the coast of Yemen and diverted it towards Somalia, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre.
UKMTO said on Thursday that it had received a report of an incident 136 nautical miles (252km) east of Yemen’s Al Mukalla, where the Seamull tanker, also known as SIBU 1, broadcast a distress call that it was being approached by an unauthorised vessel while travelling westwards in the Gulf of Aden.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items

- list 2 of 4Saudi Arabia names commander for maritime defence coalition

- list 4 of 4Saudi Arabia announces start of Red Sea defence alliance: Will it work?
“UKMTO have received confirmation that the tanker has been boarded by six armed persons who are now in control of the vessel and redirecting to Somalia,” UKMTO said in a statement.
“Authorities are investigating.
Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO.”
The maritime security monitor provided no further details and did not say whether the tanker or its crew were safe.
The Seamull tanker was sanctioned by the United States last December as one of the vessels in Iran’s “shadow fleet”, accused of exporting Iranian oil using “deceptive shipping practices” according to the the US Treasury.
It is one of four vessels operated by UAE-based Qatrat Alnada Almasi Ship Management that transported Iranian petroleum products, including naphtha and gasoil, on multiple occasions and made port calls to Houthi-controlled ports in Yemen.
The tanker was seized in one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes, as the Gulf of Aden feeds into the Red Sea and the Suez Canal, the fastest maritime link between Asia and Europe.
Roughly 12 to 15 percent of global trade by value passes through the canal each year, along with about 30 percent of the world’s container traffic.
Maritime disruptions
Piracy was rampant off the coast of Somalia in the 2000s and peaked in 2011 before being curbed by international naval deployments and new security measures for commercial shipping.
The attack follows a marked resurgence since April in Somali piracy, which had been largely dormant for more than a decade until this year.
Five cargo ships are currently held hostage – including an oil tanker that was seized in July about 26 nautical miles (48km) off Yemen’s Hadramout province.
Between 2005 and 2012, Somali pirates were blamed for more than 1,000 attacks, worth approximately $400m in ransom payments, prompting an international crackdown that all but ended hijackings in 2013.
Analysts have said that naval forces are stretched thin by conflicts in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz, causing international vessels to reroute and move closer to Somali waters.
As instability continues in the East African country, these factors have driven a renewed threat of piracy in the region.
Due to these maritime disruptions, Yemen announced on Thursday that it is creating a National Maritime Security Committee to protect shipping routes and secure navigation in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, according to Transport Minister, Mohsen Haidara Al-Omari.
The committee is to focus on protecting Yemen’s “coasts, ports, ships, securing navigation and updating legislation”, reported the SABA news agency.
This comes after Yemenis were killed and infrastructure was damaged when Houthi fighters attacked al-Makha port with missiles and drones.

polymarket-4618741.text:
Iran-backed Houthi rebels killed six people aboard a cargo ship in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Tuesday, the first reported fatalities from attacks targeting Red Sea shipping in more than a year.
Within hours, U.S.
forces said they had fired missiles at a container ship that allegedly attempted to breach Washington's blockade of Iranian ports in the Gulf of Oman.
The twin incidents illustrate how the Iran war, now in its sixth month, is inflicting a widening toll on two of the world's most critical shipping lanes.
And even as diplomats offer vague signs of progress toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz, hostilities between the U.S.
and Iran appear to be on the rise.
President Donald Trump, in an aggressively hostile Truth Social post Wednesday morning, mocked Iran's military and repeated his claim that the U.S.
has "total control over" the strait, even though traffic through it remains far below prewar levels.
"I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT!" Trump wrote of Hormuz, which was an open international waterway before the U.S.
launched the war.
The president has previously countered Iran's efforts to take control of the strait by asserting that the U.S.
will impose its own onerous tolls on passing ships, though he later dropped that plan.
"Our Naval Blockade is being called, by everyone, 'A WALL OF STEEL,' and there is nothing Iran can do about it," the president added in Wednesday's post.
"Iran is all talk and no action, the Bully of the Middle East No Longer.
Praise be to Allah!"
After the attack in Bab el-Mandeb, Yemen's Transport Ministry said the casualties included four crew members aboard the vessel — identified as the Egyptian-owned, Tanzania-flagged Tihamah — three of them Pakistani nationals and one Indonesian.
Separately, Yemen's coast guard reportedly said two members of the Yemeni government-allied National Resistance Forces were also killed in a follow-up strike as they carried out a rescue.
Yemen's Transport Ministry said in its statement that it holds "the Houthi terrorist militias fully responsible for the deaths, injuries and damage inflicted on the commercial vessel 'Tihamah' as well as for the serious consequences resulting from these attacks," according to a Google translation of Arabic.
A Houthi-aligned media outlet later said the group's forces had targeted a ship carrying Saudi military equipment, though the Houthis haven't addressed the casualty figures officially.
The Iran-aligned group declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea on July 20, breaking a yearslong Yemeni civil war truce, calling it retaliation for a Saudi "siege" on Yemen, an allegation Riyadh has denied.
Separately, the U.S.
Central Command said Tuesday that a Navy helicopter fired two missiles at the Panama-flagged Vela Nova, disabling its steering and propulsion, after the crew ignored warnings while transiting the Gulf of Oman.
Centcom said the ship had tried to run past the naval blockade Washington reimposed on Iranian ports in July.
There were no immediate reports of casualties.
U.S forces have redirected 55 commercial vessels attempting to breach the blockade since it took effect, disabled three noncompliant ships and boarded two, according to Centcom.
The hostilities at sea come as U.S.-Iran diplomacy has stalled.
Iran's Supreme National Security Council laid out sweeping demands over the weekend for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, including an end to the U.S.
naval blockade, sanctions relief, American troop withdrawals and war reparations.
Trump countered by demanding Iran pay compensation of its own.
The impasse has pushed a return to normal shipping further out of reach, even as Iran and Oman edge toward an agreement on a new transit corridor through the Hormuz Strait.
Traffic through the strait, which saw 20% of the world's oil trade before the conflict began in late February, has been barely trickling.
The war-induced tumult in the waterway has caused a global energy supply shock, sharply raising oil prices and causing broader economic consequences.
Oil prices have been rising on the back of renewed tensions.
Brent crude futures for October delivery added 0.6% to $89.44 a barrel on Wednesday, extending a rally that has added more than 7% this week, according to LSEG data.
U.S.
West Texas Intermediate for September added 0.7% to $83.8.
"Current rhetoric suggests any potential deal is still some way off, meaning risks remain skewed to the upside for oil prices," said Warren Patterson, ING's head of commodities strategy.
While there have been glimmers of progress in ongoing diplomatic efforts, few concrete details have emerged.
On Tuesday, a senior Pakistani minister told reporters that the U.S.
and Iran are close to "some sort of arrangement" over the strait, saying, "things are shaping up again in favor of a peace arrangement or a deal," Bloomberg reported.
The Pakistani official's comments came after a Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson told Al Jazeera that talks between Iran and Oman about opening a shipping channel through the Strait of Hormuz were at a "critical juncture."
Meanwhile, Turkey's Anadolu news agency reported Wednesday that Iran and the U.S.
had agreed to extend the ceasefire that ended following the collapse of the temporary memorandum of understanding weeks after it was signed in June.
But a senior Iranian source later dismissed that claim, telling Reuters that there have been no discussions with the U.S.
about extending a ceasefire under an interim deal.
The source said the U.S.
must return to the terms of the memorandum of understanding and set a time frame to implement its commitments, Reuters reported.
Correction: Centcom said the ship had tried to run past the naval blockade Washington reimposed on Iranian ports in July.
An earlier version misstated the month.

polymarket-4618741.text:
Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen have completed preparations to attack ships transiting the Red Sea's southern access point, a maritime security group led by the U.S.
Navy has warned.
"Sources close to the group stated that the Houthis have completed preparations to attack shipping, including the deployment of missiles and drones positioned near Bab el-Mandeb," the Joint Maritime Information Center, or JMIC, told mariners in a notice Tuesday.
The center, headquartered in Bahrain, provides security updates to commercial ships in the Middle East.
The European Union's naval mission in the Middle East warned Wednesday that "merchant vessels linked to Israeli, U.S.
or Saudi interests" should "avoid transiting the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden until the threat level decreases."
The Houthis have repeatedly threatened to close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait during the U.S.-Iran war.
The strait connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, the Arabian Sea and global markets.
The militants declared a maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia on Monday, threatening to cut off the kingdom's oil exports through the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb.
Those exports have acted as a crucial relief valve for global oil markets as Iran attacks tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Houthis have said "all vessels loading or discharging cargo at or from any Saudi ports are prohibited," according to the EU naval mission's notice.
Riyadh has diverted millions of barrels per day of oil through a pipeline to the Yanbu terminal on the Red Sea.
Exports from that terminal through the Bab el-Mandeb surged to 3.5 million barrels per day in June compared with just 240,000 bpd in the same period last year, according to Kpler data.
Commercial traffic has continued through the southern Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb with no attacks in the past two days, the JMIC said Tuesday.
The threat to ships in the area remains "moderate," it said.
"No changes to commercial routing or transit patterns occurred, and vessels continued to use established lanes without disruption," the JMIC said.
Ship tracking firm Kpler, however, observed a 34% decline in traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb on Tuesday compared with Monday, when the Houthis declared the embargo against the Saudis.
Four tankers with Saudi cargo turned around before reaching Bab el-Mandeb on Tuesday, according to the maritime intelligence firm Windward.
The ships are carrying 3.8 million barrels of crude oil, gasoil and naphtha, the firm said.
Iran, meanwhile, has stepped up its attacks on tankers in Hormuz as it tries to force vessels to transit the strait through its territorial waters.
Three crude oil, products and chemical tankers have come under attack off the coast of Oman and the United Arab Emirates this week.
A dozen ships have been attacked in and around Hormuz since July 6, resulting in the deaths of two seafarers and more than a dozen injuries, according to the International Maritime Organization, a United Nations agency.

Yemen’s Houthis claim missile attack on Saudi Arabia oil tanker
The Houthis recently declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea, targeting several tankers.
Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group says it has fired ballistic missiles at a Saudi oil tanker, more than a week after imposing a naval blockade on Saudi vessels in the Red Sea.
In a post on X, Yahya Saree, the Houthi military spokesman, said the group had “carried out a military operation targeting the Saudi oil tanker (NCC GHAZAL) for violating the maritime navigation ban” that the group had imposed on Saudi vessels.
He added that the group had used several ballistic missiles and forced the vessel to retreat.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), a maritime security monitor, said a tanker reported an explosion while transiting the Red Sea, adding that the crew is safe and no environmental damage was reported.
The Houthis seized the capital Sanaa in 2014 and have fought the internationally recognised Yemeni government, which Saudi Arabia backs, for more than a decade.
On July 20, the Houthis announced their maritime blockade, accusing Saudi leaders of imposing “an unjust and oppressive siege” on Yemen for nearly 12 years, “plundering our resources and imposing a comprehensive blockade”.
It went on to affirm “the right of our great people to respond to the blockade with a blockade”.
Second attack
The Houthis have also claimed an attack on two Saudi oil tankers transiting the Red Sea last week.
“We targeted two Saudi oil tankers, named Encelia and Layla, for their violation of the blockade decision issued by the armed forces,” Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said on July 22.
The Saudi Press Agency reported that the Encelia had been hit, citing an official source at Saudi Arabia’s Transport General Authority who said all crew members were safe.
The Bab al-Mandeb chokepoint connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden is one of the world’s most important shipping routes, including for oil exports.
Between Yemen to the northeast and Djibouti and Eritrea in the Horn of Africa to the southwest, the strait is just 29km (18 miles) at its narrowest point, limiting traffic to two channels for inbound and outbound vessels heading to the Suez Canal.
In 2024, about 4.1 billion barrels of crude oil and refined petroleum products passed through the strait – about 5 percent of the global total.

Ships that have avoided the waterway for several years are increasingly being tracked sailing through the international shipping waterway.
While the Houthis’ blockade on Saudi Arabia has dampened prospects for traffic growth through the Bab el Mandeb, their threats have not derailed the increasingly rapid return to the Red Sea.
Recent releases of ships hijacked by Somali pirates marks the most significant disruption of pirate networks since attacks began increasing across the Gulf of Aden and Somali Basin.
The recoveries mean five of the six vessels known to have been held by Somali pirates as recently as late August have now been freed.
The operations have underlined the ongoing risks facing merchant shipping.
Five crew members were killed on board one of the vessels, marking the first fatalities at the hands of Somali pirates in more than a decade.
The renewed tensions in the Red Sea have had a limited impact on the wider shipping industry, with the market adjusting accordingly.

Apple regained world’s top spot with $4.88 trillion valuation, overtaking Nvidia which saw a 3.5 percent market value drop.
Apple has surpassed chipmaker Nvidia as the world’s most valuable company as artificial intelligence-driven market pressures weigh on investors.
Apple is now worth $4.88 trillion compared with Nvidia’s $4.86 trillion, following a 3.5 percent decline in Nvidia’s market value.
The milestone marks the first time the Cupertino, California-based iPhone maker has held the top spot in more than a year.
